skill.name: metacognitive-guard
skill.description: Guides AI agents to recognize uncertainty, ambiguity, and complex tradeoffs, then escalate to deeper analysis when needed.
skill.summary: Helps AI agents detect reasoning struggle and escalate complex work for deeper analysis.
skill.author: ANcpLua

content.value_statement: Complex AI work can stall when uncertainty and tradeoffs are not recognized early. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a checklist for escalating difficult reasoning to deeper analysis.
actual_capabilities: Identifies high-complexity indicators such as ambiguous requirements, competing constraints, and edge case analysis.
Provides a self-assessment checklist for confidence, follow-up needs, and structured analysis value.
Shows how to request deep-think-partner assistance with context, constraints, success criteria, and a specific question.
Gives an example escalation prompt for a Redis versus PostgreSQL session storage decision.
Lists response struggle signals such as hedging, deflecting, contradiction, verbosity, and over-apology.
Guides synthesis of partner analysis into a clear recommendation and implementation plan.
limitations: It does not implement an automatic detector or run monitoring code.
It depends on access to a deep-think-partner agent or similar review workflow.
It does not replace user clarification when requirements are missing.
It is guidance-only and does not validate technical decisions by itself.

use_cases.title: Guide Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Escalate architecture decisions when performance, cost, and maintainability constraints conflict.

use_cases.title: Improve Assistant Answers
use_cases.description: Check whether a response needs deeper analysis before giving a recommendation on ambiguous implementation choices.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Escalation
use_cases.description: Define when teams should request deeper review for edge cases, integrations, or failure modes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Escalation Need
prompt_templates.prompt: Use metacognitive-guard on this question. Tell me if the task needs deeper analysis before answering: [question]

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft Answer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my draft answer with metacognitive-guard. Identify struggle signals and rewrite it with a clear recommendation: [draft]

prompt_templates.title: Frame an Escalation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for a technical decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply metacognitive-guard to this architecture choice. Decide whether to escalate, then summarize context, constraints, success criteria, and the core question: [choice]

prompt_templates.title: Plan a High-Risk Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Use metacognitive-guard for a high-risk decision. Compare possible interpretations, list missing constraints, propose an escalation prompt, and define how to synthesize the result: [decision]

output_examples.input: Should I use Redis or PostgreSQL for session storage?
output: Escalation recommended because the decision has competing constraints and operational tradeoffs.
The escalation should include current database use, traffic level, expiry needs, team skills, and cost limits.

output_examples.input: Here is a draft answer with several caveats and no recommendation.
output_examples.output: The skill flags hedging and lack of commitment. It recommends selecting one option with confidence, then asking targeted clarifying questions.

output_examples.input: Do I need deeper analysis for a simple typo fix?
output_examples.output: No escalation is suggested. The task has a narrow scope, clear success criteria, and low rework cost.

best_practices: Use the checklist before answering decisions with multiple valid approaches.
Provide context, constraints, success criteria, and the exact decision when escalating.
Synthesize partner analysis into a direct recommendation instead of forwarding it unchanged.
anti_patterns: Escalating every task, including simple edits with clear success criteria.
Using escalation to avoid making a recommendation when evidence is sufficient.
Sending vague prompts that omit constraints, context, or the actual decision.

faq.question: What does metacognitive-guard do?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants detect reasoning struggle and decide when deeper analysis is useful.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and workflow guidance; the cited examples are Markdown and YAML text.

faq.question: Does it require deep-think-partner?
faq.answer: It is designed around that agent, but the same checklist can guide any deeper review workflow.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for architecture choices, ambiguous requirements, cross-domain problems, edge cases, and decisions with high rework cost.

faq.question: Can it replace human judgment?
faq.answer: No. It improves escalation discipline, but users still need to review recommendations and constraints.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is relevant to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they support comparable delegation.
